Symbolic constants

Source: R/expressions.R
z3_const.Rd

Create named symbolic constants (the "variables" of an SMT problem). Two constants with the same name and sort in the same context are the same constant.

Usage

z3_const(ctx, name, sort)

z3_int(ctx, name)

z3_real(ctx, name)

z3_bool(ctx, name)

z3_bv(ctx, name, width)

z3_string(ctx, name)

z3_ints(ctx, name)

z3_reals(ctx, name)

z3_bools(ctx, name)

z3_fresh_const(ctx, prefix, sort)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

name

Name of the constant, a single string or a whole number (an integer symbol). For the plural forms, a character vector of names.

sort

A z3_sort, see z3_sorts.

width

Bit-vector width in bits.

prefix

Prefix of the generated name for z3_fresh_const().

Value

A z3_expr, or a named list of them for the plural forms.

Details

z3_ints(), z3_reals() and z3_bools() create several constants at once and return them as a named list.

A name may also be a whole number from 0 to 2^30 - 1, which makes a Z3 integer symbol. Z3 prints integer symbol n as k!n, but it is a different name from the string "k!n", so the two give different constants.

See also

z3_int_val() for numeric constants, z3_array(), z3_function().

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_real(ctx, "y")
p <- z3_bool(ctx, "p")
b <- z3_bv(ctx, "b", 8)
v <- z3_ints(ctx, c("a", "b", "c"))
v$a + v$b + v$c
#> <z3_expr Int> (+ a b c)
z3_int(ctx, 7L)
#> <z3_expr Int> k!7
